title: CLO International Academic Month Issue 1 (Part 2) The Application of CLO3D in Innovative Fashion Design Graduate Programs
description:
Engage with the teachers of the London College of Fashion and explore the application and learning of CLO3D in the innovative fashion design postgraduate course!

CLO3D software assists students in mastering virtual fashion design skills and fostering innovation. Students create custom fitting programs in their projects, presenting the VR filter effects of clothing online, achieving lifelike runway presentations of classical attire! Click the video to see more details!

summary: # CLO International Academic Month Issue 1 (Part 2) ## The Application of CLO3D in Innovative Fashion Design Graduate Programs --- ### Introduction Hello everyone, I'm Ella Sharp, the course leader for the MA Innovative Fashion Production course at the London College of Fashion (LCF), which is part of the University of the Arts London. Thank you, CLO3D, for inviting me to talk to you today. I'm excited to share how we use CLO3D in the MA IFP course. While our application may not encompass the entire range of CLO3D's capabilities, we utilize it for very specific purposes. ### Overview of CLO3D Usage At LCF, we employ a wide range of functions within CLO3D, which serves various teams, including buying and marketing, design, and product development. Each team uses the software differently, but these functions are interconnected. In the MA IFP, we research and develop strategies to connect these diversities effectively. ### Group Project: Capsule Collection In this particular project, students collaborated to create a capsule collection for a brand extension. They shared color and materials palettes and produced both digital and physical samples. Additionally, students were tasked with costing garments and determining production quantities. They needed to balance merchandising from both a brand-to-customer focus and a brand-to-manufacturing perspective. ### Transition from CAD to OBJ Files We have transitioned away from using CAD files and now primarily utilize OBJ files. This hybrid approach sometimes involves sending OBJ files to factories so they can inspect garment construction, such as how a facing is stitched to the lining. Our goal is to create accurate digital samples that factories can use as physical references. ### Digital vs. Physical Construction When constructing digital samples in CLO3D, we must cut the patterns and sew them digitally, which differs from the physical assembly process. This complexity requires a strong understanding of physical construction methods to ensure the accuracy of the digital sample. If the digital sample is inaccurate, the physical garment will not fit correctly. ### Sustainable Fashion Practices Our course emphasizes the importance of understanding the complete lifecycle of a product, from concept to shop floor and end-of-life considerations. We aim to visualize how products can be repurposed or recycled. The fashion industry must shift away from traditional linear practices that disconnect manufacturing from retailing. With the climate crisis as a backdrop, our teaching underscores the need for rapid innovation in the fashion sector to reduce environmental impact. ### Addressing Environmental Concerns While there are claims that virtual fashion is more sustainable than physical fashion, we must consider the energy and resources involved in digital fashion production, such as mining for precious metals and the environmental impact of digital file storage. It is a complex issue, and we must approach it with thoughtful consideration. ### Student Projects: Innovative Designs One of our recent graduates, Jai, created a full-length coat with a business model focused on disassembly and reconstruction. Her design allows customers to send back garments for reuse, embodying the modular principle. This project aligns with the Ellen MacArthur Foundation's circular economy model. ### Integrating Digital Prototyping Jai's project showcases how CLO3D can help factories and customers visualize how garments can be remade. It's essential for both students and factories to understand what garments look like inside. We encourage students to think critically about garment design and construction. ### Addressing Body Diversity Our course emphasizes the importance of body diversity in fashion design. We investigate body scanning and avatar editing to address fit issues, as a significant percentage of clothing returns are due to inaccurate sizing. CLO3D provides tools to create accurate avatars that reflect various body shapes. ### Student Innovations in Avatar Creation Students explore different scanning technologies to create accurate avatars. We teach them to import body scans into CLO3D and cross-reference with conventional tailoring measurements. This process ensures that garments fit a diverse range of body types, promoting inclusivity in fashion. ### Collaborative Digital and Physical Design Students also learn to combine digital and physical design processes. For instance, Yiran Shan created historical costumes from the Song Dynasty using CLO3D and Unity3D, showcasing how understanding physical properties enhances digital garment creation. ### Future of Fashion: Digital Twins The goal is to create accurate digital twins of physical garments to minimize waste in the production process. While challenges remain, students are encouraged to explore this evolving landscape. ### Conclusion In summary, our MA Innovative Fashion Production course at LCF leverages CLO3D to equip students with the skills needed for the future of fashion design. By combining digital and physical methodologies, we prepare our students to address the industry's challenges and contribute to sustainable practices. ### Additional Resources For more information about our course and student projects, please click on the link in the description below. --- This document provides a structured overview of how CLO3D is applied in innovative fashion design education, focusing on practical applications, sustainability, and the integration of digital and physical processes in garment design.
